title: One event through AWS Lambda
claim: Each request runs in a free execution environment, and Lambda creates a new one when none is free.
alt: A sequence with four participants: an event source, the Lambda service, a warm execution environment and a new execution environment. Two events arrive together. The first goes to the warm environment; for the second, Lambda starts a new environment and runs its initialization first.

messages.label: Two events
messages.say: An event source starts the function by direct invocation (push), or Lambda polls a queue through event source mappings (pull).

messages.label: First event
messages.say: Lambda sends the request to a free execution environment, so if a warm one is free, Lambda can reuse the environment.

messages.label: Second event
messages.say: When no environment is free, Lambda downloads your code, starts the environment, and runs the initialization code: a cold start.

messages.label: Handler
messages.say: The handler processes the event with the permissions of the function's execution role, an IAM role.

messages.label: Handler
messages.say: With standard Lambda, each environment supports a maximum of one invocation at a time, so two requests at once need two environments.
